expectations.text: States that a written agreement or reminder is not enforcement
expectations.evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md, Slack pins, and standup mentions are all rung 0 — they rely on someone remembering... No amount of restating the rule fixes this, because the rule was never wired into anything that can refuse bad work.

expectations.text: Recommends a pre-commit hook to run the formatter automatically
expectations.evidence: Pre-commit hook (fast, local) — runs the formatter and fails the commit if it's not clean.

expectations.text: Notes that pre-commit is bypassable with --no-verify and must be backed by a CI check
expectations.evidence: it's bypassable with `--no-verify`, so it's a courtesy, not enforcement... CI required check (the real enforcement)

expectations.text: Recommends a type check as a required CI check
expectations.evidence: CI required check (the real enforcement) — same formatter + type checker run in CI, wired into branch protection

expectations.text: Recommends baselining or ratcheting rather than enforcing across the whole repo at once
expectations.evidence: enforce formatting/typing only on changed files (or generate a baseline of current violations and fail only on *new* ones). The violation count can only go down from there.

expectations.text: Notes that branch protection is what makes a CI check actually required
expectations.evidence: wired into branch protection so the PR literally cannot merge if it fails

expectations.text: Recommends the failure message tell the developer how to fix it
expectations.evidence: The message should say what's wrong and give the exact fix command (`ruff format .` / `npx prettier --write .`, etc.).

expectations.text: Does not primarily recommend rewriting CONTRIBUTING.md, more reminders, or more discipline
expectations.evidence: No amount of restating the rule fixes this... focuses on gates and enforcement mechanisms, not documentation rewrites
